result.topic_en: Riemann relates an Euler-type integral function \Pi(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x) (written here as \mathfrak{F}) to his P-function P(a,b,c,x), derives the parameter relations, and lists the transformations of the P-function under sign changes of the exponents and under the substitutions x\to 1-x, 1/x, x/(x-1), etc.
result.transcription:
$\int_0^1 y^{\alpha}(1-y)^{\beta}(1-xy)^{\gamma}\,dy = \mathfrak{F}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x)$
$\mathfrak{F}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x)$ [-...-]
$\alpha+\beta+1=a \quad 2\alpha+1=a+b+c$
$\alpha+\delta+1=b \quad 2\beta+1=a-b-c$
$\alpha+\gamma+1=c \quad 2\gamma+1=c-b-a$
$2\delta+1=b-a-c$
$\mathfrak{F}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x)\,x^{\frac{\alpha+\beta+1}{2}}(1-x)^{\frac{\alpha+\delta+1}{2}} = P(a,b,c,x)$
$\mathfrak{F}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x) = P(a,b,c,x)\,x^{-\frac{a}{2}}(1-x)^{-\frac{b}{2}}$
$= \mathfrak{F}(\beta,\alpha,\delta,x)\,x^{\frac{\alpha+\beta+1}{2}}(1-x)^{\frac{\beta+\gamma+1}{2}} = P(a,-b,-c,x)$
$= \mathfrak{F}(\delta,\gamma,\beta,x)\,x^{\frac{\alpha+\beta+1}{2}}(1-x)^{-\frac{\beta+\gamma+\frac{3}{2}}{2}} = P(-a,b,-c,x)$
$= \mathfrak{F}(\gamma,\delta,\alpha,x)\,x^{-\frac{\alpha+\beta+\frac{3}{2}}{2}}(1-x)^{\frac{\beta+\gamma+\frac{3}{2}}{2}} = P(-a,-b,c,x)$
$\mathfrak{F}(\alpha,\delta,\gamma,1-x)\,x^{\frac{\alpha+\beta+\frac{3}{2}}{2}}(1-x)^{\frac{\alpha+\delta+\frac{3}{2}}{2}} = P(b,a,c,1-x)$
$\mathfrak{F}(\delta,\beta,\gamma,\tfrac{1}{x})(x-\tfrac{1}{x})^{\frac{\alpha+\delta+1}{2}}x^{\frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2}+\frac{\beta+\delta+1}{2}}$ [?] $= P(-c,-b,+a,\tfrac{1}{x})\,x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
$P(-c,-a,+b,\tfrac{1}{1-x})(1-x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
$P(-b,-c,+a,(1-\tfrac{1}{x}))\,x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
$P(a,c,b,\tfrac{x}{x-1})\,(1-x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$

$x \quad \tfrac{1}{x} \quad 1-\tfrac{1}{x} \quad \tfrac{x}{x-1}$
$x \quad 1-x \quad \tfrac{1}{1-x} \quad \tfrac{x}{x-1}$
$\mathfrak{F}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x)\,x^{\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}+\frac{2}{3}}(1-x)^{\frac{\alpha+\delta}{2}+\frac{2}{3}} = P(a,b,c,x)$
$= x^{\frac{a}{2}+\frac{1}{6}}(1-x)^{\frac{b}{2}+\frac{1}{6}}\int_0^1 y^{\frac{a+b+c-1}{2}}(1-y)^{\frac{a-b-c-1}{2}}(1-xy)^{\frac{c-b-a-1}{2}}\,dy$
$= x^{\frac{a}{2}+\frac{1}{6}}(1-x)^{\frac{b}{2}+\frac{1}{6}}\dfrac{\Pi\frac{a+b+c-1}{2}\,\Pi\frac{a-b-c-1}{2}}{\Pi a}\,F\!\left(\frac{a+b-c+1}{2},\frac{a+b+c+1}{2},a+1,x\right)$
$P(a,b,c,x)\,\Pi\frac{a+b-c-1}{2}\,\Pi\frac{a-b+c-1}{2} = P(a,b,-c,x)\,\Pi\frac{a+b+c-1}{2}\,\Pi\frac{a-b-c-1}{2}$
$P(a,b,c,x) = P(a,-b,-c,x)$
$P(a,-c,-b,\tfrac{x}{x-1}) = \mathfrak{F}(\beta,\alpha,\gamma,\tfrac{x}{x-1})\left(\tfrac{x}{x-1}\right)^{\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}+\frac{2}{3}}\left(\tfrac{1}{1-x}\right)^{-\frac{\beta+\delta}{2}+\frac{2}{3}}$
$= (-x)^{\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}+\frac{2}{3}}(1-x)^{\gamma+\frac{\alpha+\delta}{2}+\frac{2}{3}}$
$\mathfrak{F}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x) = P(a,b,c,x)$

methods.what: Definition of an Euler-type integral function of x with three parameters
Linear relations between integral exponents and P-function exponent differences a,b,c
Expressing the P-function as the integral function times power factors
Permuting integral parameters corresponds to sign changes of P-function exponents
Transformation under x -> 1-x interchanging exponents a and b
Transformations of P under the six anharmonic substitutions of x
List of the anharmonic substitutions of x
Evaluation of the integral as gamma (Pi) factors times a Gauss hypergeometric series
Relation between P(a,b,c,x) and P(a,b,-c,x) via Pi-function normalization factors
Symmetry of P under simultaneous sign change of b and c
